Rashi on Yevamot 24a:10:1.hebrew: אמרו לו ליבם - שיקום בנו על שם אחיו, דכל מצות יבום קא מודע קרא לב"ד, וקאמר להו להזהיר יבמה לבא עליה, והבן אשר תלד לו יקימנו ע"ש אחיו:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:10:1.english: Say to the yavam - That his son shall be established in the name of his brother, for the verse is informing the court of the entire mitzvah of yibbum, and is telling them to instruct her yavam to cohabit with her, and the son whom she bears to him, he shall establish him in his brother's name.

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:11:1.hebrew: אימא בכור - דוקא קאמר קרא, אבל פשוט לא לייבם לגמרי, בין איכא בכור בין ליכא בכור:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:11:1.english: Say [that] the firstborn - The verse is speaking specifically [of the firstborn], whereas an ordinary [brother] may not perform levirate marriage at all, whether there is a firstborn or whether there is no firstborn.

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:12:1.hebrew: אם כן - דפשוט לאו בר יבום הוא, למה לי דמיעט רחמנא אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו? תיפוק לי משום דלאו בכור הוא זה שנולד לאחר מיתת אחיו:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:12:1.english: If so - [that] an ordinary [non-firstborn] is not subject to levirate marriage, why do I [need] that the Merciful One excluded the wife of his brother with whom he did not coexist? Let it be derived from [the fact] that this one who was born after his brother's death is not a firstborn.

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:13:1.hebrew: ואימא - האי דמיעט אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו, כגון שהיה זה שנולד בכור לאמו ואחיו מאביו, ולהכי אצטריך למעוטי:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:13:1.english: But say - [Perhaps] that which [the verse] excluded the wife of his brother who was not in his world [was] a case where this one who was born was a firstborn to his mother, while his brother was from his father, and for this [reason] it was necessary to exclude [him].

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:13:2.hebrew: בנחלה תלה רחמנא - וממילא, בכור הנוטל פי שנים הוא דמייבם, אבל בכור לאם לא. ומדמעטיה, שמע מיניה בכור דקרא לאו דוקא, אלא גדול האחים:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:13:2.english: The Merciful One made [it] dependent on inheritance - And automatically, the firstborn who takes a double portion is the one who performs levirate marriage, whereas a firstborn to a mother does not. And since [the verse] excluded him, learn from this [that] "firstborn" in the verse is not [meant] literally, but rather [refers to] the eldest of the brothers.

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:14:1.hebrew: ואימא כי איכא בכור כו' - כלומר, דלמא לעולם בכור דוקא, והכי קאמר רחמנא: אי איכא בכור קמך, תתקיים מצות יבום או בבכור או בפשוט — דנפקא לן מדאימעיט אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו — וכי ליכא בכור, לא תתקיים, ופטורה לגמרי מן הפשוט:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:14:1.english: And say that when there is a firstborn, etc. - That is to say: perhaps [the mention of] "firstborn" is in fact specific, and this is what the Merciful One is saying: If there is a firstborn before you, the mitzvah of levirate marriage shall be fulfilled either by the firstborn or by an ordinary [brother] — for we derive [that an ordinary brother is eligible] from the fact that the wife of his brother who was not in his world was excluded — but when there is no firstborn, it shall not be fulfilled, and she is completely exempt from the ordinary [brother].

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:14:2.english: And one of them dies - [This] implies that there were only two [brothers] there, and one of them died.

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:14:3.hebrew: מי לא עסקינן - כלומר, מי לא משתמע נמי מקרא דמת בכור, וקאמר רחמנא לייבם פשוט:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:14:3.english: Are we not dealing [with] - That is to say, is it not also implied by the verse that the firstborn died, and [yet] the Merciful One says [that] an ordinary [brother] should perform levirate marriage?

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:15:1.hebrew: ואימא - על כרחך, קרא דחיק ומתוקם כגון דמית פשוט, וקאמר רחמנא לייבם בכור, דהא כתיב והיה הבכור:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:15:1.english: And say - Perforce, the verse is forced and established [as referring to a case] such as where an ordinary [non-firstborn brother] died, and the Merciful One says [that] the firstborn should perform levirate marriage, for it is written: "And it shall be, the firstborn."

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:15:2.hebrew: הא מיעט רחמנא וכו' - דהכא גבי תרי אחים כתיב מיעוט אשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו, אלמא דמית גדול משמע, ותו ליכא בכור, ומייבם קטן:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:15:2.english: Didn't the Merciful One exclude, etc. - For here, regarding two brothers, the exclusion of "the wife of his brother with whom he did not coexist" is written; thus, [the verse] implies that the older [brother] died, and there is no longer a firstborn, [and the] younger [brother performs levirate marriage].

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:16:1.hebrew: אימא כי ליכא בכור קדם הקטן זכה - דהא לא רבי דלייבם פשוט, אלא מ״ומת אחד מהם״ ומיעוט דאשת אחיו שלא היה בעולמו, דמשמע דמת בכור ואמר רחמנא לייבם פשוט. אבל איכא בכור, לא לייבם פשוט:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:16:1.english: Say that when there is no firstborn, [if] the younger [brother] went ahead, he acquires [her] - For [Scripture] only included [a provision] that an ordinary [non-firstborn] brother may perform levirate marriage from [the phrase] "and one of them dies" and the exclusion of "his brother's wife who was not in his world" — which implies that the firstborn died, and the Merciful One said that the ordinary [brother] should perform levirate marriage; but where there is a firstborn, the ordinary [brother] may not perform levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:16:2.english: Was equated, etc. - [They are] equal to perform levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:17:1.hebrew: ליהדר אגדול - אי לא בעו שאר אחיו, נחזור עליו לכופו, דמצוה עליה רמיא ולא על האחרים. אבל כי ליכא בכור, לא רמיא מצוה אגדול טפי משאר אחיו:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:17:1.english: Let [it] return to the eldest - If the rest of his brothers do not want [to perform levirate marriage], we return to him to compel him, because the mitzva rests upon him and not upon the others. But when there is no firstborn, the mitzva does not rest upon the eldest any more than upon the rest of his brothers.

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:17:2.hebrew: הולכין אצל אחיו הקטן - משמע קטן הימנו וגדול משאר אחיו, אלמא מהדרינן אגדול דגדול קודם. ומדקתני חוזרין אצל גדול, ליכא לאותובי, דאיכא למימר: מאי גדול? בכור. דאי לא מצי לשנויי הכי, אדמותיב מדתני אביי, לותיב ממתניתין, דקתני בפרק החולץ נמי: לא רצה, חוזרין אצל גדול:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:17:2.english: They go to his younger brother - This implies [one who is] younger than him and older than the rest of his brothers; thus, we seek out the eldest, for the eldest takes precedence. And from [the fact] that it teaches "they return to the eldest," one cannot raise an objection, for one could say: what [does] "eldest" [mean]? The firstborn. For if one could not answer thus, instead of objecting from what Abaye taught, he should have objected from the Mishnah, which also teaches in the chapter [entitled] HaCholetz: "If he did not wish [to do so], they return to the eldest."

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:19:1.english: Let him not take [the] inheritance - For [the word] "firstborn" is written [in the verse].

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:1:1.hebrew: ואי למ"ד - טעמא משום דאסור לבטל מצות יבמין, ואי מייבם האי חדא, דלמא מיית אידך קודם שייבם ותצא אחותה משום אחות אשה, ונמצא מצות יבמין בטלה על ידינו מיבום ומחליצה. הרי נאסרה משום כך, וכיון שנאסרה שעה אחת נאסרה לעולם. א"נ, חלץ חד לחדא ואזלא האי — השניה עומדת היא באיסור אשת אח שלא נראית ליבום מתחלה. אבל הכא, זו שנאסרה משום אחות זקוקה לאו יבמה היתה, וכי פקע איסור אחות זקוקה בחליצת אחותה, הרי זו מותרת ועומדת, דלאו אשת אח הואי. הלכך מספיקא לא מפקינן לה, דאימר כל חד וחד דידיה איתרמיא ליה:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:1:1.english: And if [it is] according to the one who said - the reason is because it is prohibited to nullify the mitzva of yevamim; for if this [brother] performs levirate marriage with one [of the sisters], perhaps the other [brother] will die before he performs levirate marriage, and her sister will be discharged on account of [being] his wife's sister, and thus the mitzva of yevamim will be nullified by our own doing from both levirate marriage and ḥalitza. Behold, she has become forbidden on account of this, and once she has been forbidden for a single moment, [she remains forbidden forever]. Alternatively, [even if] one [brother] performed ḥalitza with one [sister] and that one left, the second [sister] still stands under the prohibition of a brother's wife who was not fit for levirate marriage from the outset. However, here, this [woman] who was forbidden on account of [being] the sister of a zekuka [a woman bound by a levirate bond] was not a yevama, and when the prohibition of [being] the sister of a zekuka is lifted through her sister's ḥalitza, behold, she stands permitted, for she was not a brother's wife. Therefore, we do not remove her [from her husband] out of doubt, for one can say that each and every [brother] happened to take his own [wife].

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:2:1.hebrew: ואפילו שניהם כהנים - וחד מנייהו ודאי חלוצה נסיב, דהא ארוסת הנכרי חלוצה היא מאחד משני אחיו, כדקתני "קדמו שנים וחלצו":
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:2:1.english: And even [if] both of them [are] priests - And one of them certainly married a ḥalutza, for the betrothed of the stranger [i.e., the other man] is a ḥalutza from one of his two brothers, as [the Mishnah] teaches: "If two [brothers] went ahead and performed ḥalitza."

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:2:2.english: A chalutzah - That she is forbidden to a priest.

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:2:3.hebrew: מדרבנן הוא - והכא, דלכל חד אינה אלא ספק — דשמא זה ייבם את יבמתו גמורה — לא גזור רבנן לאפוקה מספק:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:2:3.english: It is by rabbinic law - And here, where for each one she is only a case of uncertainty — for perhaps this [brother] performed yibbum with his actual yevama — the Sages did not issue a decree to remove her out of uncertainty.

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:3:1.english: Divorced - [That is, from the verse: "And a woman divorced] from her husband they shall not take" [Leviticus 21:7].

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:5:1.hebrew: מכאן שמצוה בגדול - הכי דריש: "ולקחה לו לאשה ויבמה והיה הבכור" — המייבם יהיה הבכור:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:5:1.english: From here [we learn] that the mitzvah is upon the eldest - Thus [the Tanna] expounds [the verses]: "And he shall take her to himself as a wife and perform levirate marriage with her, and it shall be the firstborn" — the one who performs levirate marriage shall be the firstborn [i.e., the eldest].

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:5:2.hebrew: אשר תלד - ואותה יבמה תהא ראויה לילד, פרט לאילונית:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:5:2.english: That she bears - And that yevamah [widow] must be fit to bear children, excluding an aylonit [a woman incapable of bearing children].

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:5:3.hebrew: יקום - היבם על שם אחיו לנחול נחלתו, ולא יחלקו אחיו עמו:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:5:3.english: Shall be established - The levir [shall be established] in the name of his brother to inherit his estate, and his brothers shall not share [it] with him.

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:6:1.english: Do you say [it is] for inheritance - And this [word,] "he shall succeed," speaks of the yavam [brother-in-law].

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:6:2.hebrew: או אינו - אלא בבן שיולד לו משתעי, שאם היה שם המת יוסי, קורין לזה יוסי:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:6:2.english: Or is it not - rather, [the verse] is speaking of the son who will be born to him, that if the deceased's name was Yosi, they call this [son] Yosi.

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:8:1.hebrew: אין מקרא יוצא מידי פשוטו - ואע"ג דדרשינן ליה לדרשא, מידי פשוטו מיהו לא נפיק לגמרי:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:8:1.english: A verse does not depart from its plain meaning - And even though we expound it for a homiletical derivation, it nevertheless does not depart completely from its plain meaning.

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:8:2.hebrew: ואפיקתיה לגמרי - שאין צריך לקרות לבנו בשם אחיו המת, והכי גמר לה מרביה:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:8:2.english: And [it] removed it altogether - That one does not need to call his son by the name of his deceased brother, and so he learned it from his teacher.

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:9:1.hebrew: ליבם - קאמר רחמנא, "בן הנולד לך יקום על שם אחיך" מיבעי ליה:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:9:1.english: To the yavam - [If] the Merciful One is speaking [to him], He should have [stated], "The son who is born to you shall succeed in the name of your brother."

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:9:2.english: And if to the court - the Merciful One is informing [them of] the mitzvah of naming the son.

Rashi on Yevamot 24a:9:3.hebrew: יקום על שם אחי אביו מיבעי ליה - אלא ודאי ביבם גופיה משתעי קרא, ולבית דין קאמר רחמנא שיקום היבם על שם אחיו המת לנחלה:
Rashi on Yevamot 24a:9:3.english: It should have [said], “Shall succeed in the name of his father’s brother” - Rather, certainly the verse is speaking about the yavam himself, and the Merciful One is saying to the court that the yavam shall succeed in the name of his dead brother for inheritance.

Tosafot on Yevamot 24a:17:1.hebrew: ה"ג ואם לא רצה הולכין אצל אחיו הקטן - פי' אצל קטן ממנו; "לא רצה — הולכים אצל אחיו", פירוש: שאר פשוטין קטנים ממנו; "לא רצו — חוזרין אצל גדול". ויש ספרים דלא גרסי אלא "הולכין אצל קטן", ותו לא; וצריך לומר דמשמע דקטן ממנו קאמר, מדלא נקט לישנא דמתני' דהחולץ (לקמן יבמות דף לט.): "מהלכין על כל האחין":
Tosafot on Yevamot 24a:17:1.english: This is the reading: "And if he did not wish [to perform levirate marriage], they go to his younger brother" - Meaning, to one younger than him; "[If] he did not wish, they go to his brothers" — meaning, the rest of the ordinary [non-firstborn] brothers who are younger than him; "[If] they did not wish, they return to the eldest." And there are manuscripts that only read "they go to a younger [brother]," and nothing more; and one must say that it implies it is speaking of one younger than him, since it did not use the phrasing of the Mishnah in [chapter] HaCholetz (below, Yevamot 39a): "they go around to all the brothers."

Tosafot on Yevamot 24a:1:1.hebrew: אי למ"ד יש זיקה - אר"י: אע"ג דלמ"ד יש זיקה ליכא למיגזר לייבם אחר חליצה משום דלמא אתי לייבם ברישא, כדמשמע בפרק ד' אחין (לקמן יבמות דף כז: ושם) גבי רבי יוחנן דאמר "אחיות איני יודע מי שנאן", מ"מ ליכא למימר דליחלץ חד ולייבם חד, כיון דכל אחת נאסרה שעה אחת — אסורה עולמית, אפילו ראשונה, דלית ליה "יבמה שהותרה ונאסרה וחזרה והותרה תחזור להתירה" אלא לר' יוחנן; לכך הוצרך לומר "אחיות איני יודע מי שנאן". ולמ"ד אין זיקה, אף על גב דלרב דאמר אין זיקה לית ליה לקמן "כיון שנאסרה שעה" וכו', מ"מ גזרינן דלא ליחלץ חד ולייבם חד אטו דלמא מייבם ברישא, דכיון דאין זיקה — אתי למטעי ולייבם ברישא, דהא לא מסקי אינשי אדעתייהו דלמא מית אידך. אבל הכא — כל חד וחד אמרינן "אימא דידיה מתרמיא ליה", וליכא למגזר דלמא מייבם ברישא, דאפילו מייבם ברישא אימא דידיה אתרמי ליה, וכי מייבם — שפיר עבד; ומשום מ"ד אין זיקה צריך לומר כל כך:
Tosafot on Yevamot 24a:1:1.english: If [it is] according to the one who says there is a [levirate] bond - Rabbi Yitzchak says: Even though according to the one who says there is a [levirate] bond, there is no [reason] to decree [against] performing yibum after chalitzah out of concern that perhaps he might come to perform yibum first — as is implied in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Achin (later, Yevamot 27b and there) regarding Rabbi Yochanan, who said, "[Concerning the mishnah of] 'Sisters,' I do not know who taught it" — nevertheless, one cannot say that one [brother] should perform chalitzah and one [brother] should perform yibum, because once each one was forbidden for a single moment, she is forbidden forever, even the first one, for no one holds [the principle] "a yevamah who was permitted, then became forbidden, and then became permitted again, returns to her permitted state" except Rabbi Yochanan; therefore he was forced to say, "[Concerning the mishnah of] 'Sisters,' I do not know who taught it." And according to the one who says there is no [levirate] bond, even though Rav, who says there is no [levirate] bond, does not hold later [of the rule] "once she was forbidden for a moment," etc., nevertheless we decree that one should not perform chalitzah and [the other] perform yibum, lest perhaps he perform yibum first; for since there is no [levirate] bond, he might come to err and perform yibum first, because people do not keep in mind that perhaps the other [brother] will die. But here, [regarding] each and every one we say, "Say that his own [wife] happened to come to him," and there is no [reason] to decree lest he perform yibum first, for even if he performs yibum first, say that his own [wife] happened to come to him, and when he performs yibum, he acted properly; and because of the one who says there is no [levirate] bond, [the Gemara] needed to say all this.

Tosafot on Yevamot 24a:2:1.hebrew: וספק חלוצה לא גזרו בהו רבנן - הקשה הר"ר משה ברבי יעקב מפיה"ם, דאמר בהחולץ (לקמן יבמות דף לו:): "מת בתוך ל' יום — אם אשת ישראל היא חולצת, ואם אשת כהן היא אינה חולצת". ולמה לא תחלוץ, כיון דספק חלוצה מותרת לכהן? וי"ל דהתם, שחולצת לאחר נשואין, יאמרו קמו רבנן במילתא דנפל הוה, ולכך הוצרכו חליצה, ואתי למישרי חלוצה לכהן; אבל הכא, כל אחד כשכונס, אמרי' קים ליה להאי דלאו חלוצה היא, ולכך כנסה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 24a:2:1.english: "And [in a case of] uncertainty [as to whether she is] a ḥalutzah, the Sages did not issue a decree" - Rabbi Moshe ben Rabbi Yaakov of Piham raised a difficulty, for [the Gemara] says in [chapter] HaḤoletz (below, Yevamot 36b): "[If a child] died within thirty days — if she is the wife of an Israelite, she performs ḥalitzah; and if she is the wife of a priest, she does not perform ḥalitzah." But why should she not perform ḥalitzah, since a woman of uncertain ḥalutzah status is permitted to a priest? And one can answer that there, where she performs ḥalitzah after marriage [to the priest], [people] will say that the Sages ascertained the matter [and determined] that it was a non-viable infant, and therefore they required ḥalitzah, and [consequently, people] will come to permit a [definite] ḥalutzah to a priest. But here, when each one marries [his wife], [people] will say [that] this one knows for certain that she is not a ḥalutzah, and that is why he married her.

Tosafot on Yevamot 24a:6:1.hebrew: או אינו אלא לשם - ויהא כוליה קרא כפשטיה, ולא נדרוש מ"בכור" דמצוה בגדול לייבם, אלא ה"ק: "והיה הבכור" — פי' הראשון שתלד היבמה — יקרא שמו בשם המת. ויליף בג"ש דלאו שם ממש קאמר, אלא לנחלה. וכיון דלנחלה קאמר, ליכא לאוקומי קרא אלא ביבם; דאי על הבכור שתלד היבמה קאמר קרא שיקום על שם המת לנחלה, שאותו בכור יירש את המת — דאם כן, "יקום על שם אחי אביו" מיבעי ליה, דהשתא לא שייך למימר דה"ק "אמרו ליה ליבם", כדקאמ' בסמוך:
Tosafot on Yevamot 24a:6:1.english: "Or [perhaps] it is only to [inherit] his name" - And [thus] the entire verse would be [understood] according to its plain meaning, and we would not derive from "the firstborn" (habekhor) that the mitzvah is upon the eldest [brother] to perform levirate marriage; rather, this is what [the verse] is saying: "And it shall be that the firstborn" — meaning, the first [child] whom the yevamah bears — shall be called by the name of the deceased. And [the baraita] derives through a verbal analogy (gezerah shavah) that [the verse] does not mean an actual name, but rather [that it refers] to inheritance. And since it refers to inheritance, the verse can only be established [as referring] to the yavam; for if the verse were speaking about the firstborn whom the yevamah bears, that he shall succeed in the name of the deceased for inheritance — [meaning] that that firstborn shall inherit the deceased — [that cannot be,] for if so, it should have said "he shall succeed in the name of his father's brother," since now [in that case] it would not be applicable to say that [the verse] means "Tell the yavam," as [the Gemara] says shortly [below].
